question: How much of a player's RAPM is reconstructed by a linear combination of their six-factor ratings, per season?
inputs: 1Y regular-season impact-ratings-v1-method fits for 2014-15 to 2025-26 (RAPM and six factors from the same fit)
method: Sample: players qualified for RAPM and for all six factors in the season's 1Y fit.
Second stage: weighted least squares of RAPM (total) on oTS, oTOV, oREB, dTS, dTOV, dREB with an intercept, weights = player seconds.
Also reported: ORAPM on oTS, oTOV, oREB and DRAPM on dTS, dTOV, dREB.
uncertainty: Player bootstrap (200 resamples of the qualified players, seed 2501) for each R2.
evaluation: In-sample weighted R2 (the figure comparable with the commonly quoted 0.985)
Cross-season R2: coefficients fitted on season t-1 applied to season t
acceptance: All three R2 values reported for all twelve seasons (cross-season from 2015-16)
limitations: The six factors are rate models with their own denominators and penalties; they are not additive to RAPM by construction
A high in-sample R2 with six inputs and a few hundred players can overstate out-of-sample fit
negative_result_policy: Publish the measured R2 values whatever they are, including if they fall well below 0.985.
